summary: Production hardening for the memory substrate: crash-recovery, concurrency, store-level write_plane truth, and a post-migration consolidation dry-run. All four acceptance predicates PASS with observed evidence; every claim was adversarially re-verified by five independent skeptics (all CONFIRMED, 48 independent test re-runs green). Delivered WITHOUT editing any peer-claimed file (W3-STORE/KIND/VEC own moneta_store.py + store.py) by routing store-health via read-only introspection and running the dry-run through Moneta's read-only classify(). SEAM GUARD: HEAD == fix/memory-store-recovery == 5e933c13, zero drift.
env: Python 3.14.2, Windows; moneta importable, pxr (OpenUSD 0.26.5) importable — real-USD + real-store hardening is OBTAINABLE, not UNKNOWN.

acceptance.predicate: kill-mid-write then reopen: root parses, last durable memory readable, no corruption
acceptance.anchor: tests/test_w3_harden_crash_recovery.py (5 tests). test_hard_kill_at_replace_instant_preserves_last_durable spawns a real subprocess that os._exit(137) INSIDE a patched os.replace at the 2nd deposit (returncode==137, banner absent) -> reopen==['mem_A']: root parses, last durable readable, B (interrupted) not corrupting. Mechanism: Moneta durability.snapshot_ecs writes tmp->fsync->os.replace (atomic) [C:/Python314/Lib/site-packages/moneta/durability.py:108-116]; per-deposit save() [moneta_store.py:445-456]; reopen _quarantine_if_corrupt before Moneta's bare json.load hydrate [moneta_store.py:319-350]. Adversarial P1: CONFIRMED (regression to a direct in-place write fails the test).
acceptance.limitation: Process-kill durable, not power-loss durable: snapshot_ecs fsyncs the tmp fd but issues no directory fsync after os.replace. Out of scope for the 'kill-mid-write' predicate; must not be read as power-loss-durable.

acceptance.predicate: two concurrent writers: both memories present afterwards, observed merge semantics receipted
acceptance.anchor: tests/test_w3_harden_concurrency.py (5 tests). OBSERVED, not asserted from USD docs: (a) in-process 2nd handle on same URI -> MonetaResourceLockedError (single-owner) [moneta/api.py:199]; (b) USD layer-merge: two memories in two distinct sublayers compose into cortex_root and BOTH prims survive on real pxr Stage.Traverse() (non-tautological: deleting the subLayerPaths line empties the traverse); (c) two sessions SERIALIZED through the single-owner lock -> survivors==['mem_sessionA','mem_sessionB']; (d) same-file two writers do NOT merge (disk-byte observation). Cross-process boundary receipted (finding F1). Adversarial P2: CONFIRMED, no holes.
acceptance.limitation: 'Both present' holds for the store's real single-owner-serialized access pattern and for USD sublayer composition. Genuinely-concurrent cross-process store writers CAN clobber (survivor read is ECS-snapshot last-writer-wins; USD sublayers do not feed it) — see finding F1; fix scoped to W3-STORE.

acceptance.predicate: doctor write_plane ok is demonstrably derived from store-level evidence
acceptance.anchor: tests/test_w3_harden_write_plane_store.py (10 tests) + probe. write_plane.store_health() reads the LIVE store object (store._global_synapse.store, the same singleton the bridge serves via get_synapse_memory) READ-ONLY — never constructs a store — and derives degraded from: serving CLASS vs requested backend (catches jsonl-serving-while-moneta even when the fallback flag is None/reset), count() reachability, and Moneta durable-layer/engine-handle presence [python/synapse/server/write_plane.py]. Folded into write_plane_state()'s verdict; surfaced in the doctor via _check_write_plane_store() wired into run_doctor [doctor.py]. CRUCIBLE SEAM pinned: test_healthy_bridge_stays_true_when_store_is_degraded proves _handle_get_health returns healthy=True while write_plane.status=degraded (healthy is a liveness answer, not derived from write_plane). Adversarial P3+P5: CONFIRMED (4/5 degraded shapes flag; wired to real Moneta internals _handle:191/.durability:601/count:501).
acceptance.limitation: store_health is NON-MUTATING by module contract (a health probe must not write), so a Moneta store with intact _handle/durability/count() but a silently-failing save() reads ok — the dir-writability probe is the designated write-capability check. Closing this needs a store-side _last_save_ok telemetry flag (spawn S2, W3-STORE).

acceptance.predicate: post-migration evolve dry-run returns a sane audit over the real corpus
acceptance.anchor: tests/test_w3_harden_evolve_dryrun.py (5 tests). Non-destructive consolidation audit via Moneta's OWN read-only classify() [moneta/consolidation.py:99] — NOT run_pass, which 'still prunes' in dry-run [consolidation.py:143]. test_dry_run_over_real_corpus_is_sane_and_non_mutating opens a copytree copy of the REAL on-disk corpus (.synapse/corpus/.moneta/snapshot.json, 39 rows, dim 256) with a dim-matched HashEmbedder(256), runs the audit -> sane (count_before==39, projected==before-len(prune), lists), ZERO mutation (snapshot bytes byte-identical across the audit, id-set + count unchanged). Non-triviality pinned by test_dry_run_detects_prunable_without_removing. The existing synapse_evolve_memory dry_run branch pinned structurally non-mutating. Adversarial P4: CONFIRMED (classify source-verified read-only).
acceptance.limitation: The audit skips decay to stay non-mutating, so it reports snapshot-time utility, not current-time; on the healthy real corpus this yields prune=0. Non-triviality is covered by the synthetic prunable test. 'sane' = internally consistent + zero-mutation, not 'reflects a fully-decayed pass'.

findings.claim: Moneta's single-owner URI lock is PROCESS-LOCAL (an in-memory _ACTIVE_URIS set; the error says 'in this process'). Two separate OS processes opening the same store dir BOTH open, and the whole-ECS snapshot is last-writer-wins -> a deposit is silently CLOBBERED. Observed live: two subprocesses deposited, reopen showed 1 of 2 survivors.
findings.disposition: Fix (a cross-process owner lock) belongs to W3-STORE, which owns from_storage_dir + the nine-store unification per the SEAM GUARD. W3-HARDEN receipts the observation and spawns the fix (S1). Bus finding posted (nonce 18cb754337319f60). Acceptable single-user-localhost bound today; a prerequisite for any multi-session deployment.

findings.claim: The spec's §0 'ONE ROOT CAUSE' is LIVE in this base: the real corpus stores 256-dim vectors, the default SemanticEmbedder emits 384-dim, and Moneta init eagerly rebuilds the vector index -> ValueError: embedding dim mismatch: expected 384, got 256. So the real corpus CANNOT be opened under the default backend here. This means W3-DIM (Phase 0) has not landed in my base.
findings.disposition: Out of W3-HARDEN scope (W3-DIM owns the dim fix). The consolidation dry-run does NOT use vectors (classify reads utility/attended_count/state only), so the real-corpus audit runs by matching the reader dim to the corpus (HashEmbedder(256)) — a legitimate way to read existing data. Once W3-DIM lands, the real corpus opens under the default backend and write_plane goes degraded->ok as the spec predicts.

spawn.name: cross-process owner lock for the Moneta store (silent clobber -> loud refusal)
targets: from_storage_dir writes a .moneta/OWNER lockfile (pid+host, O_CREAT|O_EXCL); a 2nd LIVE same-host owner is REFUSED loudly instead of clobbering; a dead-pid/stale lock is reclaimed; same-pid reentrant; removed on close(); FAIL-OPEN on any lock-internal error (never block a legitimate single-session open).
